subject: Close cadence: bridging procurement impasse & provisional staging
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Kim <natalie.kim@opalhealth.com>, Opal Health Procurement <procurement@opalhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Close cadence: bridging procurement impasse & provisional staging

Hi Natalie / Opal procurement team —

Quick update from our side as we prep for the evaluation close later this month. There are two items we want to surface and propose a fast path for:

1) Legal review timeline looks like it may push the close beyond the target date (we saw similar delays on other health ops deals).
2) A few procurement questionnaire items are asking for evidence (SOC2 logs + retention controls) that take time to line up.

Attached is a lean MAP draft (MAP-draft-v2.pdf) and a short procurement checklist (procurement-checklist.xlsx) that maps the minimal artifacts we need to unblock a go/no-go decision. Proposed next steps:

- Can your legal/procurement team confirm the expected turnaround for the outstanding items by EOD tomorrow?
- If review will exceed five business days, would Opal consider a provisional staging MOU restricted to non-production data so we can begin integration and early validation while legal finishes the standard contract?
- We can offer a short-term SLA credit during staging as a goodwill measure; Sean (CC) will weigh in if we need an exec exception.

Goal: avoid a hard close slip by giving Opal ability to validate in staging while legal completes the contract. If staging is not acceptable, we need to agree on a re-baselined timeline this week so our teams can realign resources.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call this afternoon.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.pdf (pdf), procurement-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Natalie Kim <natalie.kim@opalhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Opal Health Procurement <procurement@opalhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-14T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close cadence: bridging procurement impasse & provisional staging

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear plan. A couple of constraints from our side:

- Our legal team flagged an indemnity and data-processing appendix that requires a standard review cycle; historically that takes ~10 business days for our counsel if there are redlines.
- Procurement needs the vendor questionnaire item #7 (third-party pen test summary) AND confirmation of retention windows for logs before they can approve production access.

We do like the idea of a provisional staging MOU for early validation, but two asks before we can sign anything provisional:

1) A one-page scope limiting processing to pseudonymized test data;
2) A short-term liability cap aligned with our enterprise rules (we can share a template).

If Redwood can provide those two items by EOD tomorrow, I will escalate to our legal lead to fast-track a provisional sign-off. Otherwise, we should expect a formal close delay and we need a revised MAP with new milestones.

Natalie Kim
Director, IT Procurement | Opal Health
natalie.kim@opalhealth.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-14T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Proposed bridge options for OPAL close cadence

Team — looping you in with an exec-level ask: Opal's note above creates a likely 10-business-day legal review that will push the close into September unless we provide a bridge. We should treat this as a close-risk escalation and move one of the following paths today: 

Option A — Provisional staging MOU (preferred):
- Limited scope (pseudonymized/test data only), 30-day provisional term, explicit liability cap and audit window.
- Redwood provides a staging SLA credit (1 week pro-rated) and an expedited SOC evidence package.

Option B — Re-baseline MAP with milestone escrow:
- Push close date by 3 weeks; sign an interim milestone letter with payment cadence tied to delivery gates.

Option C — Technical escrow + early access with controlled sandbox and no production data.

I am authorizing the team to offer a modest acceleration credit for Opal if it helps secure staging sign-off this week. Marissa — please draft a one-page provisional scope and an updated MAP timeline that covers both the preferred staging flow and a fallback re-baseline. Ben — push the procurement checklist and the minimal SOC extracts; Laura — coordinate with Legal to prepare the provisional MOU template.

Attached: risk_log_20250814.csv — quick entries capturing the procurement blockers and mitigation options.

I want a clean recommended route by 3pm PT so we can present a single path to Natalie and her legal lead.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Close cadence: bridging procurement impasse & provisional staging

Thanks Sean — that escalation is helpful and appreciated. I reviewed the three options with our lead counsel and procurement:

- We are open to Option A (Provisional staging MOU) provided Redwood returns the one-page scope and the liability cap language by EOD tomorrow. If we receive the documents, I will push our counsel to triage and aim to sign the provisional MOU this week.
- As a contingency, procurement agrees to a re-baselined MAP (Option B) with a target close of 2025-09-02 and milestone payments if we cannot complete the provisional sign-off.

Action items I will own: expedite counsel review once we have the one-page scope and liability cap.

If Redwood sends the draft scope now, I will route it internally and confirm whether we can land the provisional MOU sign-off this Friday. Appreciate the quick pivot.

Best,
Natalie Kim
Director, IT Procurement | Opal Health
